From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Jared Lee <jared.lee@fintechco.com>

Subject: FintechCo - Logging & Redaction follow-up

Hey Sam / Jared,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful to understand your ingestion patterns and the types of fields you need redacted before we persist logs. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap
- Scope: API request/response logging for our external inference calls (customer-facing app). You want selective logging of telemetry while ensuring PII and sensitive tokens are never persisted.
- Examples called out: account numbers in request payloads, personally identifiable fields (SSN, DOB), auth headers / session tokens, trace IDs that could map back to customers.
- Retention: 30 days for debug traces, 90 days for aggregated metrics. You may want shorter retention for raw request payloads.
- Residency: primary constraint is that logs must remain in us-east-1 for regulated product lines.
- Controls: need the ability to mask/redact at ingest, remove headers, and opt-out for specific customer IDs.

Proposed next steps
1) I attached a short doc (redaction_controls_v1.pdf) that outlines Redwood’s logging control primitives: field-level redaction rules, header stripping, trace ID hashing, and retention policies.
2) Can you confirm the top 5 sensitive fields you want redacted (we heard: account_number, email, ssn, full_name, payment_token)?
3) We’ll route this to our SE (Vivek) and security lead if needed to surface the exact implementation and any SOC2 implications.
4) If acceptable, we’ll provide a sample config + a short demo (10–15m) showing how redaction rules apply to a sample request stream.

Open questions from our side
- Do you need deterministic pseudonymization for trace IDs (i.e., same trace mapped to same token for debugging) or full irreversible hashing?
- Any contracts / procurement timeline we should be aware of?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Vivek for technical detail.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Marissa,

Thanks — high level looks good. A few clarifications from our security and platform teams:

1) Trace IDs: we prefer deterministic pseudonymization so we can stitch traces for a single session across services, but the mapping must be reversible only by our ops team (we can provide a KMS-wrapped key). If Redwood supports KMS-wrapped reversible pseudonymization we are interested; otherwise strong one-way hashing is acceptable for audit logs.

2) Retention: For raw request payloads containing PII we need a max retention of 7 days unless explicitly approved. Aggregated metrics and counters can be 90 days.

3) Headers: We need the option to drop Authorization and Cookie headers entirely from logs. App-level IDs (x-request-id) can be hashed.

4) Data residency: All logs for our regulated products must stay in us-east-1 and not be replicated to any eu/apac regions. Is that configurable per-customer?

5) SLAs: if we provide redaction rules and a test dataset, how quickly can Redwood implement and verify masking in a staging environment?

We can share the exact list of fields tomorrow. Also copying Procurement to loop in on timelines.

—Sam
Sam Walker
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo

Marissa / team / Sam — quick technical note and recommended next steps.

Short answers
- KMS-wrapped reversible mapping: We can support deterministic pseudonymization using a customer-supplied KMS-wrapped key. Implementation will apply an AES-GCM envelope with per-tenant key material so mapping is deterministic but access-controlled. This satisfies your "reversible only by ops" requirement.
- One-way hashing: supported (SHA-256 + salt) for audit logs where irreversibility is desired.
- Headers: We already have header-stripping at the ingestion gateway; we can add per-customer header blacklists (Authorization, Cookie) and per-header hashing for things like x-request-id.
- Data residency: We can scope log persistence to a single region (us-east-1) per customer. That will prevent replication to eu/apac.
- Retention: Our retention engine supports per-tenant rules. We can set raw request payloads with PII to 7 days and aggregated metrics to 90.

Estimate & next steps
1) Technical doc + sample config: I’ll generate a sample redaction config (field patterns, header rules, pseudonymization) and post it to the Drive link by EOD Monday. (See: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xExampleDocId/view?usp=sharing)
2) Staging validation: We can roll the config to staging and run a 2-day validation with your sample dataset. ETA: 3–5 business days from sign-off.
3) Security review: If you want reversible mapping via customer KMS, our security team will need the KMS policy to validate access patterns. That typically adds 2 business days for a SOC2-compliance-friendly review.

Deliverables
- sample_redaction_config.json (config + examples)
- staging validation report (logs pre/post masking)
- runbook for key management and support contacts

If that timeline works, Marissa — can you confirm and share Sam's final list of fields and any procurement constraints? Sam — happy to jump on a short technical call if helpful.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
